assumptions: The flag revert is credited with the recovery because the service returned to baseline about a minute after it, not because any independent test isolated the flag as the cause.
The rollout ramp (a 60-of-200 slice at 16:53, fully on from 16:54) is inferred from the per-minute flag evaluation counts in the logs, not from the flag provider's rollout configuration.
Only io-shop's own metrics, logs and change events were examined; no check was made for knock-on effects on upstream or downstream services, so impact is assumed to be confined to the account page.
The specific trigger condition (an empty collection passed to max(), e.g. an account with no statement data) is inferred from the exception text and stack location; it has not been reproduced.

Shoppers are assumed to have seen a failed account page rather than incorrect data, based on the errors being unhandled exceptions.
input.executive_summary: For roughly six minutes on 27 September 2026 (16:53–16:59 UTC), the account page of the online shop failed for a substantial share of shoppers who tried to load it. The cause was a newly switched-on feature that was released behind a toggle; the new code behind it could not handle accounts with no spending data and returned an error instead of a page. Shoppers who hit the problem would have seen the account page fail to load and would generally have succeeded on a retry once the fix was in; other parts of the shop, including browsing and checkout, were not implicated. The automated on-call system detected the problem, traced it to the newly enabled feature, and switched the feature back off within about a minute of being alerted, after which the page recovered and stayed healthy. A draft code fix has been opened for engineers to review before the feature is enabled again. Impact figures quoted elsewhere in this report come from the shop's own measurements over the outage window.
input.root_cause: Enabling the `monthly-spend-feature` flag on io-shop at 16:53:00Z exposed a new code path in `src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:627` that calls `max()` on a collection that can be empty, raising an unhandled `ValueError` and failing account page requests; as the flag ramped from a 60/200 slice to fully on, the share of failing requests rose with it. Turning the flag back off at 16:59:01Z removed the code path and the service returned to baseline.
